dimensions.assessment: Affects federal immigration officials, regional centers, state and local government economic development officers, and mayors.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall establish within U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services an EB-5 Regional Center Program Advisory Committee.

dimensions.assessment: Advisory and consultative role that makes recommendations but does not alter direct benefit adjudications or statutory EB-5 rules.
dimensions.evidence: The Advisory Committee shall advise, consult with, report to, and make recommendations to the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services

dimensions.assessment: Prohibits committee members from receiving federal pay or benefits for their service, limiting fiscal impact to administrative support costs.
dimensions.evidence: The members of the Advisory Committee may not receive pay or benefits from the United States Government by reason of their service

dimensions.assessment: Adds a single advisory committee and associated subcommittee structure to the Homeland Security Act of 2002.
dimensions.evidence: Subtitle E of title IV of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Establishes operations that continue until the final adjudication of all benefits filed under the EB-5 Regional Center Program.
dimensions.evidence: The Advisory Committee shall be terminated upon adjudication of all benefits filed under section 203(b)(5) and 216A of the Immigration and Nationality Act

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes an advisory committee within U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services to provide recommendations on the EB-5 Regional Center Program, involving periodic reporting, briefings, and structured stakeholder representation.

label: H.R. 6992
